source_text:
ἐποχούμενον ἅρματι, οὐκ ἐπὶ γῆς ἀτάκτως ἐλαύνοντα, ἀλλ' αἰθερίους δρόμους
καινοπρεπῶς ἀναστέλλοντα, καὶ τὸν οὐράνιον καμπτῆρα καταλαμβάνειν
ἐπειγόμενον, καὶ τὸν παρατρέχοντα Βελίαρ δυνατῶς καταστρέφοντα. 43.481 Ἀλλ'
Ἰουδαίων παῖδες οἱ βάσκανοι τῆς ἀληθείας ἀκούσαντες, ὅτι ὁ Χριστὸς ἀνελήφθη εἰς
οὐρανοὺς, ἀμαυρῶσαι βουλόμενοι τὸ παράδοξον θαῦμα τοῦ Ἡλίου τῆς δικαιοσύνης,
τὸν Ἠλίαν παρεισάγουσι λέγοντες· Τί μεγάλα κομπάζετε, Χριστιανοὶ, ὅτι ἀνελήφθη
ὁ Χριστὸς, ὡς λέγετε; Καὶ γὰρ Ἠλίας, ἄνθρωπος ὢν, τῆς ὁμοίας δόξης ἀξιωθεὶς
ἀνελήφθη εἰς οὐρανούς.
Πρὸς οὓς μετὰ παῤῥησίας φθεγξόμεθα· ∆ιὰ τί, ὦ Ἰουδαῖοι, τὰς βίβλους ὡς
τυφλοὶ σκυλεύετε, καὶ τὰ γεγραμμένα ἐν αὐταῖς μετὰ ἀκριβείας οὐ βλέπετε; ∆ιὰ τί
ἀναγινώσκετε, καὶ οὐκ ἐπιγινώσκετε; Τί γάρ φησιν ἡ θεία Γραφή; Καὶ ἀνελήφθη
Ἠλίας ἐν συσσεισμῷ ὡς εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν· τὸ δὲ, ὡς εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, ἀμφίβολον ἔχει
τὴν ἔννοιαν· τὸ δὲ, εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, τρανὴν δείκνυσι τὴν ἀλήθειαν. Ὅτι δὲ οὔτε
Ἠλίας, οὔτε ἕτερός τις ἀνέβη εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ
καταβὰς ὁ μονογενὴς τοῦ Θεοῦ Υἱὸς, αὐτὸς περὶ ἑαυτοῦ πάντας πληροφορῶν λέγει·
Οὐδεὶς ἀναβέβηκεν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, εἰ μὴ ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβὰς, ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ
ἀνθρώπου, ὁ ὢν ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ· ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλὸς, ὁ τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα τῶν
ἀγγέλων πρόβατα καταλιπὼν ἐπὶ τὰ οὐράνια ὄρη, καὶ τὸ πεπλανημένον πρόβατον
εὑρηκὼς, καὶ ὤμοις φιλανθρωπίας βαστάζων, καὶ εἰς τὸν οὐράνιον λιμένα
ἀνενεγκὼν, τῷ ἰδίῳ Γεννήτορι δωροφορῶν φθέγγεται· Εὗρον, Πάτερ, τὸ πρόβατον
τὸ πλανώμενον, ὅπερ ὁ ἀπατεὼν ὄφις δολοτρόποις τεχνάσμασιν ἠπάτησε, καὶ
κακίας ὁδοὺς ὑπέδειξε, πηλῷ δὲ τῆς πολυθεΐας τὴν καθαρότητα τῆς θεογνωσίας
ἐμόλυνε. Θεασάμενος οὖν αὐτὸ ἐν τῷ βορβόρῳ τοῦ βίου πνιγόμενον, τῇ τῆς
θεότητός μου δεξιᾷ ταχέως ἀνήρπασα· καὶ τοῖς τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν σπλάγχνοις ἐν τοῖς
τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ῥεύμασιν ἀπέπλυνα, καὶ μυρίσας τῇ εὐωδίᾳ τοῦ ἁγίου μου Πνεύματος,
διὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως νῦν παραγέγονα, ἄξιον τῆς σῆς θεότητος προσκομίζων σοι
ξένιον, τὸ λογικὸν πρόβατον.
Σήμερον ὁ διάβολος τὴν οἰκείαν ἧτταν ὀδύρεται, ὁρῶν τὸ ἡμέτερον σῶμα εἰς
οὐρανοὺς ἀναγόμενον· σήμερον ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἀναλήψεως τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ
ὡς καπνὸς διαλέλυται· σήμερον ὁ διάβολος θρηνεῖ λέγων, Τί ποιήσω, ὁ ἄθλιος;
Πάντας τοὺς ἀπ' αἰῶνος ὡς ἱέραξ ὀξυπετὴς ἁρπάξας παρ' ἐμοῦ, ἔρημόν με κατέστησε,
καὶ πανταχόθεν με πτεροκοπήσας εἰς γῆν κατέῤῥαξεν.
thought_title: Elijah taken as into heaven, Christ truly ascended
orientation: The preacher finishes his chariot image of Christ in flesh going to heaven, then answers Jewish objectors who cite Elijah, then gives Christ as shepherd presenting the found sheep to the Father as the devil starts to lament.
pass_a_gloss: riding in a chariot, not driving in disorder upon earth, but in a strikingly new manner sending up ethereal courses, and hastening to seize the heavenly turning post, and with power overthrowing the devil running alongside. But the children of the Jews, the maligners of the truth, having heard that Christ was taken up into heavens, wishing to dim the strange wonder of the Sun of righteousness, bring in Elijah saying: Why do you boast great things, Christians, that Christ was taken up, as you say. For Elijah also, being a man, having been deemed worthy of like glory, was taken up into heavens. To whom with boldness we shall speak: Why, O Jews, do you plunder the books as blind men, and do you not see with exactness the things written in them. Why do you read, and do you not fully know. For what does the divine Scripture say. And Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind as into heaven. But the phrase as into heaven holds a doubtful meaning. But the phrase into heaven shows the clear truth. And that neither Elijah nor any other one went up into heaven, except alone the only begotten Son of God who came down from heaven, he himself assuring all concerning himself says: No one has gone up into heaven, except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of man, the one who is in heaven, the good shepherd, the one who left the ninety nine sheep of the angels upon the heavenly mountains, and found the wandering sheep, and carries it on shoulders of love for humanity, and brought it up into the heavenly harbor, offering a gift to his own Begetter speaks: I found, Father, the wandering sheep, which the deceiving serpent deceived with crafty devices, and showed ways of evil, and with mud of many gods stained the purity of knowledge of God. Therefore having seen it drowning in the mire of life, with the right hand of my Godhead I quickly snatched it up. And with bowels of compassions in the streams of the Jordan I washed it clean, and having anointed it with the fragrance of my holy Spirit, through the resurrection now I have come, bringing to you as a gift worthy of your Godhead, the sheep endowed with reason. Today the devil mourns his own defeat, seeing our body being led up into heavens. Today sin through the ascension of Christ Jesus has been dissolved as smoke. Today the devil laments saying, What shall I do, wretched that I am. Having snatched all those from ages past from me as a swift flying hawk, he made me desolate, and having clipped my wings on every side he dashed me down to earth.

lemmas.gloss: riding upon, borne in a chariot

choices.why: Race image requires a rival running beside the chariot whom Christ overthrows, and παρατρέχω means run beside or past, not attack.

choices.english: in a strikingly new manner sending up ethereal courses
choices.why: ἀναστέλλω here directs upward and launches the ascent, matching hastening to seize the heavenly turning post, not holding back.
λογικόν means possessing logos or reason, said of humanity, and periphrasis avoids the misleading paradox of rational sheep while keeping the sense.

choices.term: ὡς εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν contrasted with εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν
choices.english: as into heaven contrasted with into heaven
choices.why: The argument turns on ὡς making the Elijah text doubtful and indirect, while the bare εἰς states the clear truth of Christ, so both small words must stay.

choices.term: ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλὸς ... δωροφορῶν φθέγγεται
choices.english: the good shepherd, the one who left ... offering a gift, speaks
choices.why: Brief voices mark this as Christ himself speaking while offering, continuing from the Son of man saying, so it must remain apposition to the speaker, not a new third person sentence.
rejected: He is the good shepherd, who left

pass_b_english: riding in a chariot, not galloping in disorder across the earth but launching his course through the upper air in strikingly new glory, pressing on to round the heavenly turning post and mightily striking down the devil running beside him. But when the children of the Jews, begrudging the truth heard that Christ was taken up into the heavens, they wanted to dim the astonishing miracle of the Sun of Righteousness, so they bring in Elijah against us with these words: “Why do you Christians boast so loudly that Christ, as you say, was taken up? Elijah too was a man, counted worthy of the same glory, and he was taken up into the heavens.”

To them we answer boldly: “Why, O Jews, do you plunder the books like blind men and fail to see exactly what is written in them? Why do you read without understanding? For what does the divine Scripture say? ‘And Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind as into heaven’ (2 Kings 2:11). That ‘as into heaven’ leaves the meaning doubtful, while the bare ‘into heaven’ shows the clear truth. Neither Elijah nor anyone else has gone up into heaven, but only the only-begotten Son of God who came down from heaven, and he gives us full assurance about himself when he says, ‘No one has ascended into heaven except he who came down from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven’ (John 3:13), the good shepherd who left the ninety-nine sheep of the angels on the heavenly mountains, found the wandering sheep, carried it on the shoulders of his love for humanity, brought it up into the heavenly harbor, and as he offers his gift to his own Father cries: ‘Father, I have found the wandering sheep, which the deceiving serpent tricked with treacherous devices, led into ways of wickedness, and stained the purity of the knowledge of God with the mud of many gods. I saw it drowning in the mire of this life and quickly snatched it up with the right hand of my divinity. With tender mercy I washed it in the streams of the Jordan and anointed it with the fragrance of my Holy Spirit, and now through the resurrection I have come, bringing to you a worthy gift for your Godhead, the sheep endowed with reason.’”

Today the devil mourns his own defeat as he watches our body carried up into the heavens. Today sin is scattered like smoke by the ascension of Christ Jesus. Today the devil wails and says: “What shall I do in my misery? Like a keen-swooping hawk he snatched from me all the people of every age, left me desolate, clipped my wings on every side, and dashed me to the ground.”

problems.why: Adds 'flesh' as subject, absent from the source; the Greek participles (ἐλαύνοντα, καταστρέφοντα) are masculine, so the rider is Christ, not feminine σάρξ.
problems.ruling: Source has ἐποχούμενον ἅρματι only; no σάρξ. Masculine participles ἐλαύνοντα, καταστρέφοντα imply Christ, not invented 'flesh' subject.

problems.quote: the spiteful children of the Jews
problems.source_quote: Ἰουδαίων παῖδες οἱ βάσκανοι τῆς ἀληθείας
problems.why: Omits τῆς ἀληθείας ('of the truth'), turning a polemic against begrudging the truth into a generic insult.
problems.fix: the children of the Jews, begrudging the truth,
problems.ruling: English drops τῆς ἀληθείας from οἱ βάσκανοι τῆς ἀληθείας, losing envious-of-the-truth force of the polemic.

fixed: 'flesh riding' misstates masculine ἐποχούμενον / ἐλαύνοντα / καταστρέφοντα (rider is Christ): removed added 'flesh'.
'spiteful children of the Jews' omitted τῆς ἀληθείας: restored as 'begrudging the truth' to govern βάσκανοι.
